rationale: The original records an intended use for loose stools in an oral mixed-spice preparation. It provides no separate constipation response or dose attribution to nutmeg.

The constipation subscale was measured, and the publication identifies diarrhoea as the only statistically clear change. A numerical constipation effect estimate was unavailable and the tested exposure was extracted carrot fiber.
An original entry describes externally applied grated nutmeg in a mixture intended to aid sleep. It contains no observation after oral intake and no Parkinson sleep comparison.
This pilot used orange-derived fiber snacks and tracked microbiota and proteins. There was no constipation severity comparison after raw orange consumption.
